key_insight: Edit3r is a feed‑forward model that reconstructs and applies instruction‑aligned 3D edits from sparse, unposed, view‑inconsistent images in a single pass—removing the need for per‑scene optimization or pose estimation.
problem_solved: Eliminates slow, per‑scene optimization and the requirement for posed, multi‑view consistent inputs by enabling instant, photorealistic 3D scene edits from sparse, unposed image sets.
method: Feed‑forward 3D reconstruction+editing network that directly predicts instruction‑aligned edits from sparse, unposed, view‑inconsistent images (no pose estimation or per‑scene optimization).

Training strategy that compensates for the lack of multi‑view consistent edited supervision via region extraction (e.g., SAM-based masks), synthetic multi‑view augmentation and consistency-aware supervision to teach the model multi‑view coherence.
Design focused on photorealistic rendering and single‑pass inference to produce multi‑view consistent edited scenes quickly at test time.
impact: Enables fast, scalable 3D scene editing workflows for content creators and researchers by converting sparse, in-the-wild image edits into coherent 3D results without expensive optimization or pose labeling. This lowers the barrier for AR/VR content creation, rapid prototyping, and interactive editing.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: sparse unposed images + text instruction → Edit3r feed‑forward model → multi‑view edited 3D render outputs (single‑pass).

paper_title: Edit3r: Instant 3D Scene Editing from Sparse Unposed Images
paper_authors: Jiageng Liu, Weijie Lyu, Xueting Li, Yejie Guo, Ming-Hsuan Yang
